text:
maria: Quick sync — I sketched a Q3/Q4 plan for a 'regional shielding' initiative (routing policies + multi-tenant isolation + graceful cross-region failover). Want product + infra + ops eyeballs before we hand to sales. TL;DR: phase 1 = tenancy-aware routing + opt-in residency; phase 2 = affinity + canary/fallback lanes; phase 3 = full SLA+billing alignment.

alex: link to the doc?

maria: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROD-REG-SHIELD — section 2 has acceptance criteria and a rough timeline.

jin: High level ask from a couple enterprise customers: they want per-tenant residency controls, predictable latency window (p95) per region, and a fast evacuation/fallback path with audit logs. We should call that out as must-have for Dedicated customers.

sam: +1. For launch gating I propose three criteria: 1) telemetry + SLA measurement (p95, error rate) 2) rollback policy verified (canary -> instant fallback) 3) at least one pilot customer on Dedicated and one on Hosted that opt-in.

jess: Telemetry specifics: need per-tenant route-change rate, end-to-end latency p50/p95, KV-cache hit ratio, and cross-region egress bytes. Also add prompt-quality regression hooks tied to eval sets (so we don't degrade model quality during routing fallbacks).

kyle: Ops note — capacity planning: we should phase by tier. Tier A (enterprise) gets affinity lanes and guaranteed capacity, Tier B gets soft-affinity and best-effort. Start canaries in a single region with reserved capacity pools before we expand multi-region.

maria: Sounds good. I'm adding a short rollout playbook. Draft snippet for the canary rollout policy:

```
- canary: 5% traffic from pilot tenants routed to region-B variant
- monitor: p95 latency > baseline + 50ms OR error_rate > 0.5% => rollback
- duration: 2h steady state, then 15m ramp to 25% if stable
- fallback: automatic routing to primary region and alerting to oncall
```

alex: What's the expected impact on egress costs? Need a crude model for sales. If we do cross-region failover by default customers may incur unexpected charges. Suggest an opt-in checkbox for cross-region failover that surfaces cost delta.

maria: Agreed — adding cost-awareness and a UI/contract flag. Also plan to surface quantization/compute tradeoffs per tenant for cost optimization.

jin: Security/compliance: include KMS integration and per-tenant audit events for routing decision changes. For regulated customers we should allow explicit VPC-only path with no cross-region egress.

sam: Timeline?

maria: Proposal: Q3 — discovery + pilot (canary policy validated, telemetry in place). Q4 — phased rollout to Tier A, Dedicated first. Shipping date tentative; moving to product sprint planning next week.

jess: One more ask: we need a simple test harness for route failover to run during oncall drills. Make that part of the acceptance criteria.

kyle: Ops will own the drill playbook once implemented. I'll volunteer to run the first drill with infra.

deploy-bot: New doc created: PROD-REG-SHIELD (maria) — watchers: infra, prod, sales.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll update the ticket with the suggestions and create an action list for sprint planning.

alex: We should also schedule a 30-min handoff with solutions engineering to prep customer comms.

maria: Done. Scheduling invite now. :calendar:
